conviction_note: Mixed evidence: an industry pricing proxy (CPI car rental +9.1% YoY in Sept) points to an RPD beat against the company's 'roughly flat' Q3 RPD guide, while summer TSA volume (-2.7%, Aug -4.4%), softening used-car values and a FY guide ($850M-1B adj EBITDA) whose low end needs H2 +20% YoY against a street Q3 EPS below last year point to a cut that analysts are already pricing (PTs cut to $115/$105/$95, stock -33% since 7/30). A crowded short (~13% of shares out, roughly 30%+ of float after SRS's ~49%, 12 days to cover) and a +9% 5-day run-up give squeeze risk on anything not bad, but the name has risen after only 1 of its last 7 prints. So p_up 46 on a 10-point abs move gives -0.8, and the findings sum to -0.8: both measurements lean slightly down, and the evidence does not support a strong sign.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $8.28-$8.75 (Benzinga $8.28/$8.34, Chartmill $8.63, Earnings Whispers $8.75; https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CAR/earnings-forecasts , https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CAR/estimates , https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/CAR), revenue $3.41-3.46B (Q3 2025 $3.519B, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723612/000072361225000076/a03-pressreleasexq3f25.htm). Company guide: FY2026 adj EBITDA $850M-$1.0B reiterated 2026-07-28, Q3 RPD 'roughly flat' YoY, Americas fleet down mid-single digits (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/summaries/CAR-2Q26-AI-Summary). Q3 or FY adj EBITDA consensus could not be sourced, so the guidance bar is inferred, not sourced, and the findings that depend on it are capped small. The three EPS sources roughly agree (5% spread). FY2026 EPS consensus $2.71 (stockanalysis) does not reconcile cleanly with the quarterly numbers.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 4,586,856 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 11.99 days to cover, down from 5.25M on 9/30 and a 9.03M peak on 3/31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/car/short-interest). That is 13.0% of the 35.3M shares outstanding. SRS Investment Management held 17.4M shares in Q1 2026 (~49%, https://www.holdingsintel.com/filers/0001503174/positions/CAR), so the short is likely 30%+ of free float. This is a crowded short with a squeeze history (52-week high ~$843 in an April 2026 squeeze, now -84%). Skew is +8.3 vol points (25-delta puts over calls), so the option market pays for downside. Put/call OI is 0.68 and total OI only 1,356, with the ATM spread at 54% of mid, so the 9.14% implied move is indicative only. The stock is +9.07% over 5 days and -1.04% over 20. Sell-side cut targets into the print: Barclays $160->$115 EW (2026-11-02), JPM $145->$105 UW (2026-10-08), MS $99->$95 EW (2026-09-11) (https://www.stockanalysis.com/stocks/car/forecast/).

findings.finding: BLS CPI for car and truck rental was +9.1% YoY in September 2026 (+0.1% MoM), while Avis guided Q3 RPD to 'roughly flat' YoY on the Q2 call. If even a third of that industry pricing reached Avis's Americas RPD (Q3 2025 $73.19), the Q3 revenue/RPD bar ($3.41-3.46B, which embeds flat RPD and fewer days) would be beaten.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The name sells prints: 1 up of the last 7 (median |move| 6.8%). On Q3 2025, revenue beat estimates with RPD -1% ex-FX and the stock fell 6.06% (baseline; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/avis-budget-stock-declines-11-despite-reporting-q3-earnings-beat). On Q2 2026, record utilization and flat RPD gave -6.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Neither the company guide nor the consensus revenue (down 2-3% YoY) carries any RPD uplift. If the market had priced a pricing beat, the stock would not be -33% since 7/30 with analysts cutting targets into the print, and the skew would not be +8.3 put-rich. The caveat: CPI rental also includes truck rental and did not track Avis's flat Q2 RPD, and Avis is deliberately shifting mix toward longer, lower-RPD rentals, so it is filed as a proxy and sized small.
findings.independence: Separate sources point to travel-price inflation from the 2026 fuel shock: Delta domestic unit revenue +16% in Q3 (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx?type=bn), and Hertz Q2 2026 RPD +9% YoY (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001657853/000165785326000045/q22026earningsrelease.htm). The secondary source has not been checked against the BLS table.

findings.finding: TSA checkpoint volume for June 21-Sept 7 2026 was 204.15M against 209.91M a year earlier (-2.7%), with August -4.4%, as fuel-driven airfares rose (Delta Q3 adjusted unit revenue +15%, United revenue +17.4% on 1.3% capacity). Fewer air travellers means less airport rental volume, Avis's core channel.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume misses have been sold. On Q2 2026, rental days fell 2% with bookings trailing expectations and the stock fell 6.9% (baseline; https://www.autorentalnews.com/news/avis-cuts-fleet-as-summer-demand-trails-expectations).
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (summer 2026 analysis; page fetch returned 403, figures from the search snippet)
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly inside the guide: the company already guided the Americas fleet down mid-single digits for Q3 and said summer bookings trailed expectations. What may not be priced is that August, the peak month, fell harder (-4.4%) than the July run-rate the company could see when it spoke on 7/28. If the market had fully priced it, revenue consensus would sit nearer -4% than -2-3%.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Corroborated by Avis's own Q2 call ('inbound travel fell below initial expectations', https://www.autorentalnews.com/news/avis-cuts-fleet-as-summer-demand-trails-expectations). The fare data comes from the airline 8-Ks/RTTNews, a different source.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of $850M-$1.0B adj EBITDA (reiterated 2026-07-28) needs H2 of at least $677M after H1 of $173M, against H2 2025 of $564M (Q3 $559M + Q4 $5M), i.e. +20% YoY. Street Q3 EPS of $8.28-8.75 sits below Q3 2025's $10.11, so the street appears to carry less than the guide low end, and a guide cut on 11/03 is the likely forward line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025: a guide miss ('fell significantly short of guidance') with an $800M-1B 2026 guide gave -21.54%. Q1 2026: the guide was raised to $850M-1B and the stock still fell 14.7% (per a coverage headline; baseline shows -0.47% close-to-close). Q2 2026: the guide was reiterated and the stock fell 6.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The stock is -33% since 7/30 (https://www.trefis.com/stock/car/articles/621253/can-avis-budget-stock-fall-50/2026-10-29), Barclays cut its PT $160->$115 on 11/02, JPM $145->$105, MS $95, and skew is put-rich. What is unpriced is the size: a cut to roughly $750-800M sits near where the street EPS implies, while a cut below $750M or a hold would surprise. The bar is not sourced (no EBITDA consensus found), so this is capped small and the wide range carries the uncertainty. Shrunk for the crowded short.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 figures come from a separate document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723612/000072361225000076/a03-pressreleasexq3f25.htm), and Q4 2025 $5M/FY2025 $748M from the Q4 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723612/000072361226000010/a03-prxpressreleasexq4f25.htm). The analyst PT cuts are a second, independent signal.

findings.finding: The Manheim index fell to 205.9 in September 2026 (-0.6% YoY, -1.1% MoM; non-adjusted -1.2% YoY), the first YoY decline of 2026. Cox cut its year-end forecast from +2% to +0.2%, and the least fuel-efficient vehicles fell most. Mid-October recovered to 207.4 (+2.2% YoY, +0.7% MoM). Weaker residuals raise Q4 per-unit fleet cost against the FY $315-325/month guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025: 'unfavorable used vehicle pricing' plus aggressive defleeting gave adj EBITDA of $5M and -21.54% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723612/000072361226000010/a03-prxpressreleasexq4f25.htm). Q2 2026 per-unit fleet cost of $292 (-4%) was not rewarded (-6.9%).
findings.why_not_priced: The release is public and cushioned: the FY DPU guide of $315-325 already implies H2 near $340 against Q2's $292, so modest softening may sit inside the guide. That is why it is small. It is filed because the Q4 2025 collapse came from exactly this line, and the October mid-month rebound partly offsets it.
findings.independence: Mid-October data from the same publisher (https://www.autobodynews.com/news/manheim-index-rises-0-7-in-early-october-as-wholesale-supply-tightens) points the other way. Gasoline at +37.6% YoY (finding on fuel) explains the fuel-inefficient segment weakness.

findings.finding: Avis received $650M cash from Pentwater on 2026-10-05 (Section 16(b) settlement, to be recognised in Q4). On 2026-11-02 it noticed redemption of all $350M of its 5.750% 2027 senior notes for 2026-12-30, about $20M of annual interest. This supports the stated target of cutting net corporate leverage by at least a full turn from 7.4x by year-end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The settlement news gave an overnight rise of 5.22% when announced (https://www.itiger.com/news/1104931090). No print reaction history on leverage.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: both 8-Ks are public. What the money buys is debt reduction, not a ramp. What may be unpriced is the call's update of the leverage path and any buyback or further redemption from the remaining ~$300M. If priced fully, the 10/06 pop would not have faded into a -33% drawdown. The gain is a one-off below operating income, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: The 2026-10-06 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723612/000095014226002687/eh260839574_8k.htm) is the same company source. The Q2 call states the leverage target (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/summaries/CAR-2Q26-AI-Summary).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-21 Avis's AESOP fleet ABS issued $650M of five-year Series 2026-5 notes: Class A $474.5M at 5.69%, Class D at 8.14%. This is routine fleet funding at rates that keep vehicle interest elevated in an inflationary (3.7% CPI) environment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to fleet ABS issuance.
findings.why_not_priced: What the money buys: refinancing of the domestic fleet, with no distress signal, so it is near zero. Its only edge is that Q4 vehicle-interest guidance could edge up. If it were a signal, the ABS would have priced wide or been upsized, and it was not reported that way.

findings.finding: The short is crowded: 4.59M shares (Oct 15 settlement), 13% of shares outstanding and likely 30%+ of free float given SRS's ~17.4M shares, with 12 days to cover. The stock ran +9.07% in the 5 sessions into the print while the shorts fell 667k shares in the first half of October. Any guide that is not a deep cut has squeeze fuel.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2026 squeeze to a ~$843 52-week high and then an unwind (https://rallies.ai/news/avis-budget-slides-as-short-squeeze-unwind-accelerates-after-jpmorgan-downgrade). Despite the short, 6 of the last 7 prints fell.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is public, so this is a mechanism, not a secret. It makes the reaction asymmetric to a sell-side that has cut targets into the print (lowering the bar). If the squeeze were priced, call skew would be bid. Instead skew is +8.3 put-rich and OI is tiny (1,356).
findings.independence: SRS holding: https://www.holdingsintel.com/filers/0001503174/positions/CAR. PT cuts lowering the bar: https://www.stockanalysis.com/stocks/car/forecast/.

findings.finding: International adj EBITDA fell 11% to $73M in Q2 2026 on weaker demand and more fleet supply in several European markets. Q3 is International's seasonal peak (Q3 2025 International adj EBITDA $190M vs $139M), so a repeat of the Q2 decline would cost about $20M against a high comparison.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 international weakness was part of the -6.9% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because it was disclosed in Q2. Q3 2025's +37% International comparison is a tough lap that previews do not spell out. Sixt, the European peer, has not reported Q3 2026, so no independent Europe read exists. Net of the rest: the Americas is ~70% of EBITDA and drives the print.
findings.independence: none (the Sixt Q3 item found was 2025, rejected).

findings.finding: Ravi Simhambhatla, EVP and Chief Digital & Innovation Officer, left effective 2026-09-30 (8-K 2026-09-01) after selling 4,702 shares at ~$138-140 on 2026-08-07. Housekeeping, with no successor named.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial; filed for completeness. A loss of digital leadership matters only if the call discusses tech or Waymo programmes.

findings.finding: US regular gasoline averaged $4.36/gal in September 2026, +37.6% YoY (diesel at a record $6.29), and AAA called it the highest ever for the time of year. That weighs on drive-leisure rental demand and on residuals of the less fuel-efficient fleet, and raises shuttle and operating fuel cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Avis print under a comparable fuel shock in this baseline.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (BTS September 2026 motor fuel release; figures via search snippet)
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro transmission the company has not confirmed. Renters pay their own fuel, and high airfares could push some trips into rentals, so the sign is uncertain. It is filed small as a proxy. If priced, airline-like fuel sell-offs would already show in CAR, and they partly do (-33%).
findings.independence: AAA: https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/ ; Delta fuel cost commentary (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx?type=bn). This overlaps the TSA finding only through airfares, a separate mechanism.

outside_window.finding: Hertz reports Q3 2026 at 08:00 ET on 2026-11-05, after the exit window closes on 11-04, so its RPD/DPU read-through cannot reach this trade. Its Q3 guide was adj corporate EBITDA $275-325M, transaction days +1%, DPU $285-295.
$350M 2027 notes redemption settles 2026-12-30. The cash effect is after the window; the notice itself is filed in findings.

baseline_tension: The negatives (guide risk, volume, residuals) agree with the +8.3 put skew and the -33% drawdown since July, so they are largely priced. The positives (CPI pricing, crowded short, a sell-side bar cut into the print, +9% 5-day run-up) cut against the skew. Net, the findings lean slightly against a negative call, and p_up sits near 50 rather than at the skew's implied lean.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, ~30%+ of float, 12 DTC): shrank the negatives: guidance -1.5 to -1.1, TSA volume -1.0 to -0.8, fuel -0.4 to -0.3; p_up 45 to 46.
Lesson 1 (this name sells prints, 1 up of 7): CPI pricing finding +1.2 to +1.0.
Lesson 2 (one-off): Pentwater cash is below operating income with a path only to leverage, so financing +0.5 to +0.4.
Lesson 6 (bar): EPS bar sourced to three roughly agreeing aggregators; FY EBITDA consensus unsourced, so the guidance finding stays capped small with a wide range.
Lesson 5 (proxy): CPI, TSA and gasoline findings left small and marked as proxies; none dropped.
